definitions.explanation: A door consisting of panels that rotate around a central axis, commonly found at the entrances of hotels, office buildings, and department stores. Also used figuratively to describe a situation where people cycle in and out repeatedly.

examples.japanese: ホテルの{入|い}り{口|ぐち}に{回転|かいてん}ドアがある。
examples.english: There is a revolving door at the hotel entrance.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{回転|かいてん}ドアに{挟|はさ}まれないように{注意|ちゅうい}した。
examples.english: I was careful so the child wouldn't get caught in the revolving door.

examples.japanese: この{会社|かいしゃ}は{離職率|りしょくりつ}が{高|たか}く、まるで{回転|かいてん}ドアのように{人|ひと}が{入|はい}れ{替|か}わる。
examples.english: This company has a high turnover rate — people cycle through like a revolving door.

notes:
{回転|かいてん} means 'rotation' or 'revolving,' and ドア is the loanword for 'door.' {回転|かいてん}ドア refers to the rotating entrance doors found in large buildings. Like in English, the term is also used metaphorically to describe rapid turnover of people in organizations or positions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {回転|かいてん}ドアを{通|とお}る (to go through a revolving door)
- {回転|かいてん}ドア{式|しき} (revolving-door style)
- {回転|かいてん}ドアの{入|い}り{口|ぐち} (revolving door entrance)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自動|じどう}ドア — automatic door (slides open automatically; much more common in Japan)
- {引|ひ}き{戸|ど} — sliding door (traditional Japanese-style door)
